thread:
Noah Blake: quick assist pls — new engineer running the quickstart gets a 403 on the very first API call. sample app logs: {"error":"billing_required", "message":"workspace billing not set up"}. They accepted the invite email and can see the workspace in the web UI.

Tara Singh: did they sign up via SSO or direct invite? also, which token are they using (user vs service)?

Noah Blake: direct invite. They started the sample with a repo .env that contains REDWOOD_API_KEY=REDACTED and REDWOOD_WORKSPACE_ID=ws_personal.

Ivy Chen: quick checklist: 1) confirm which workspace the token is scoped to (`redwood tokens inspect <token>` or `curl /v1/whoami`), 2) check `redwood whoami` to see CLI cached workspace, 3) ensure the workspace actually has an active payment method or trial enabled.

Noah Blake: ran `curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/whoami | jq .` and got "workspace_id": "ws_org123", "billing_status": "unpaid". That's different from REDWOOD_WORKSPACE_ID in their env.

Tara Singh: aha — token-scoped workspace (ws_org123) > env var. Service tokens are locked to a workspace and will hit that workspace even if REDWOOD_WORKSPACE_ID points elsewhere. If that workspace is unpaid you'll get billing_required.

Noah Blake: ok, how did the token become tied to the unpaid org? the token was created by our infra team.

Ivy Chen: infra often auto-creates workspaces; billing is a separate manual step. If infra generated a service token scoped to the infra workspace, it will surface this exact failure when that workspace lacks a payment method.

Noah Blake: what's the fastest unblock?

Tara Singh: options: (A) rotate the token to one scoped to a paid workspace, (B) create a personal sandbox workspace from Profile -> Create workspace and use a personal API key for dev, (C) have an org admin add a payment method to the infra workspace. For immediate dev speed, (B) is usually quickest.

Noah Blake: spun up a personal workspace and replaced the token with a personal key. re-ran the quickstart and got a first successful response: 
```json
{"id":"resp-1","status":"ok","output":"hi"}
```

Noah Blake: notes for the quickstart docs: - call out that API keys/service tokens are bound to a workspace and override REDWOOD_WORKSPACE_ID - show `curl /v1/whoami` and `redwood tokens inspect` examples in troubleshooting - explain SSO vs invite vs terraform-provisioned workspace billing caveats - improve the billing_required error to include a direct Console -> Billing link and a one-line next step (add card or use personal sandbox)

Ivy Chen: +1 on the error payload. Also add a short snippet for Docker/sample-app: "confirm env token matches the intended workspace" — we see many folks mount the wrong secret into containers.

Tara Singh: I'll file a small DX ticket for the payload change and the tokens inspect snippet.

DevEx Bot: Ticket created: DX-4600 "Quickstart: clarify token workspace scope, add whoami/tokens inspect snippets, and include billing link in billing_required response" :white_check_mark:

Noah Blake: thanks all — resolved for the new hire, closing thread.
